posts.name: chioma christopher
posts.cooked:
Hi everyone I’m Chioma, a builder in the CKBuilders program. I’ve been building Crowns, a real-time 3D car race where players put CKB on the line and the chain decides who won. It’s live on testnet, and I’d love for you to race it and tell me what you think.

Play: https://keepers-relay.vercel.app (testnet)
Code: GitHub - Kaylahray/keepers_relay: Crowns: live 3D car races on Nervos CKB. 2–5 players race 3 laps for a shared pot; each phone signs its own moves, and the chain replays the whole race before paying the winner. Rust rules on CKB-VM and in WebAssembly, Spore trophies, testnet. · GitHub
Build thread: Crowns: a live multiplayer skill game where CKB-VM replays every run · Issue #45 · Nervos-Community-Catalyst/CKBuilder-projects · GitHub

image1350×563 307 KB

image1326×627 118 KB

image1304×658 80.8 KB

Why I built it

In most online games with money on them, you have to trust the server. It holds the money, it decides who won, and you can’t check either. I wanted a fast, real-time game where nobody has to be trusted: not me, not the server. The chain holds the money and replays the race itself before it pays anyone.

What it is

A race for 2 to 5 players: 3 laps, everyone driving at the same time, with items, boosts and crashes. Races come in two kinds:

  • Entry races: everyone puts in the same entry fee in CKB, and the winner takes the whole pot.
  • Sponsored races: the host puts up the prize and you join free. You only lock a deposit for your seat, and it all comes back after the race.

In the game:

  • 3 tracks: Harbour Loop (the fast one), Switchback Hill (tight hairpins) and Old Town (narrow streets), each with its own scenery.
  • 8 items from pads on the road: Ram, Slick, Jolt, Barricade, Crown Rush, Ward, Patch and Draft. Crashes and hits cost health, and a wrecked car stops for a moment before it rejoins.
  • Phone or computer: on a phone, touch the left or right side of the screen to steer, with buttons for boost and brake. On a computer, use the keyboard.
  • Free practice against two bots on the same rules, with no wallet.
  • Trophies: win a race and claim a trophy, a Spore you own. You can only get one for a race you really won, and the CKB inside it stays yours.
  • Profiles: claim an @username, which is a cell you own on chain. Upload a picture or pick a ready-made look, and it’s minted as a Spore you own and set as your profile picture. Your trophies, wins and crown shards show on your profile and on the leaderboard.
  • Replays: anyone can open a finished race, see each driver’s time, shards and moves, and watch it again in 3D, rebuilt from the moves stored on chain.

How a race works

  1. Host: someone opens a race and picks the track, the number of seats and when it starts (5 to 60 minutes). They either set an entry fee, or sponsor a prize and let players in free.
  2. Join: players take a seat. Each player who joins takes a fifth off the time left.
  3. Start: when the clock reaches zero, everyone is taken into the race at the same moment, with a 10-second countdown.
  4. Payout: when the race ends, the winner is paid automatically. If nobody finishes, everyone gets their money back, and a sponsor gets their prize back.

Your wallet only asks you once, when you join. While you race, your browser signs your moves with a temporary session key, so there are no popups mid-race.

How CKB makes it fair

  • No one holds the money. The host’s CKB sits in a match cell and each player’s in their own seat cell, all locked by the match script, live-match. Not me, not the server.
  • The chain is the referee. The finish transaction carries every car’s moves. live-match spawns the game script with ckb-script-ipc and calls it like a function: judge(record) replays the whole race tick by tick and returns each car’s place. Only then does live-match pay out.
  • Nobody can fake a win. Each player’s moves are signed by their own session key, and the script checks the winner’s signature. The race server (a small relay) passes moves between phones in real time, but it can’t invent them.
  • Money can’t get stuck. If the relay disappears, every entry can go back to its owner after a timeout the chain enforces, with nobody else’s signature.
  • Sponsored races can’t be farmed. Joining one needs a username cell in your wallet, which the chain checks through a cell dep, and the chain refuses one wallet taking two seats in a prize race.
  • One set of rules everywhere. The race rules are one Rust crate with integer maths only, compiled to RISC-V for CKB-VM and to WebAssembly for the browser and the relay, so all three always agree on who won.
  • Anyone can check it. The results page reads the moves from the finish transaction, replays the race in your browser and checks it against who the chain paid.

Status on testnet

  • live-match (type ID): 0xcf2c00c07441a48baeb76284e8edb8d10c6e016865c3eb6b1f87ad3b57a146b7
  • Latest upgrade, sponsored races (22 Nov): 0x4e13e90f…57d4
  • First sponsored race: a 100 CKB prize, and the winner got their deposit back plus the prize. 70,475,122 cycles: 0x8e3bca44…f623
  • A close entry race on 23 Nov: won by 1.5 seconds with 251 signed moves, and the whole race was replayed on chain before paying 200 CKB. 65,322,821 cycles: 0xcef2e225…d515
  • 49 transaction tests in ckb-testtool on the real RISC-V binaries, plus an OffCKB devnet test of seven full races with a real relay and bot drivers.

The cycle counts above are the chain’s own. You can check them yourself: paste either hash into ckb-cycle-tools. It replays the finish in your browser and splits it per script: for the 23 Nov race, live-match and the game it spawns are 63.5M of the 65.3M (97.3%), and the replay matches the node’s total exactly. The worst case (5 cars, full 3 minutes, twistiest track) is about 141M in my tests.

Things I learned on CKB

  • Spawn and IPC make a game a library. live-match doesn’t know anything about racing. It only asks a game script “who won?”. Any game that serves the same trait could use the same match script and its money rules.
  • Same result everywhere needs integer maths. One float anywhere and the phone and the chain would disagree. Fixed ticks and integer maths keep the browser, the relay and CKB-VM in step.
  • Profile the spawned script on its own. In a spawn, the match script is the parent (VM 0) and the game is a child (VM 1), so a plain profile only sees the parent. With ckb-debugger --vm-id 1 and ckb-cycle-tools, which can profile a spawned script on its own, I found that about half of the game’s cycles go to one function that finds the nearest point on the track. That’s where my next cut goes.
  • A cell dep is a free check. The sponsored-race username pass is read as a cell dep, so it costs the player nothing and the cell isn’t spent.
  • Signing live moves needs ordering. I found that key presses sent as separate web requests could reach the relay out of order. The phone then refused to sign a list it didn’t recognise, and a winner could lose the prize. Now each phone has one WebSocket, and every press is numbered.

What it doesn’t do yet

  • One relay. Only my relay runs races today. It can’t cheat, but if it’s down, races wait for the timeout refund.
  • Reload mid-race: a driver who reloads gets back into the race, but can’t sign the moves made before the reload yet.
  • Usernames are checked as free by the app before you claim one. Making that fully on chain is next.
  • Looks: each car is just its seat’s colour. Car skins you own as Spores, richer environments and real car models are next.

What I’d love feedback on

  • How does racing feel on your phone? Is the steering responsive, and is the lag OK?
  • Is anything confusing for someone new to CKB?
  • About half the replay is a nearest-point search on the track. Has anyone made a search like this cheaper in CKB-VM?
  • Each phone signs its moves with a session key, and the chain checks only the winner’s signature before paying. Do you see a gap in that, or a more CKB-native way to do it?

It’s on testnet. Look for the gold Free entry races: you can join those without paying anything. Or grab some testnet CKB from the faucet and host your own, and share the link with friends: it shows a preview card of the race.

Thanks for reading!

posts.name: Enzo
posts.cooked:
Well done.

The game is smooth on my phone though I only played in practice mode.

Maybe add some bot player for the paid race?

posts.name: chioma christopher
posts.cooked:
Sorry for the late reply, and thanks for trying it! Glad it runs smoothly on your phone.

I’ve thought about bots for paid races. In a paid race, all the CKB comes from the players, so a bot racing for that money would need someone’s wallet behind it, and that someone would be me. I’d be betting against my own players, and I don’t want that. The whole idea of Crowns is that the chain is the referee and nobody has an edge, including me.

What I might add later is bots that fill empty seats so a small race feels fuller. They’d be part of the game rules, so the chain drives them during its replay, but they’d never put in an entry or win the pot.

For now, the way to try a real race without paying is a sponsored race, the host puts up the prize and you join free (look for the gold Free entry badge on the Races page). You just need a username.

I’m planning to host one soon. Would you join if I post the time here?

posts.name: Thinker
posts.cooked:
看完了项目介绍，除去复杂的技术细节，单从产品落地的角度，我有两点比较现实的担忧：

  1. 真金白银奖池下的外挂风险： 纯娱乐大家图个开心，但一旦涉及真实的奖金，规则透明的竞速游戏很容易引来脚本外挂，普通手动玩家在现金局里可能根本没法玩下去。

如果无法避免，那其实可以考虑直接引用AI赛道，在赛道里加入一些随机数障碍，增加外挂预判的难度，就让大家跑自己AI。

  1. 多人匹配的冷启动难度： 2到5人同时在线匹配，以目前 CKB 生态的日活体量，前期赛程可能比较难凑齐人，容易出现等待过久的问题。

建议可以增加单人AI赛道娱乐模式，让玩家随时上线都能先跑起来，把基础活跃度撑住。

关于社区与 DAO 支持的想法：

对完成度很高 、且没拿社区资助完成的优质应用类项目，如果早期冷启动应该比较困难，感觉DAO资金可以适当支持下，帮助其冷启动（如此项目自行完成度很高情况下，可以考虑做它几期的赞助赛事主办方来来看下社区活跃效果）。

其实建议DAO资金可以适当考虑向应用类项目倾斜下，这样既能帮优质项目顺利度过冷启动期，也能适当地激活一下社区氛围。你们感觉呢 @zz_tovarishch @Hanssen

posts.name: zz_tovarishch
posts.cooked:
感谢对 Crowns 的建议，也感谢 at 我。不过我发现最近 DAO 和 Spark 经常被放在一起讨论，虽然他们都是被放在 DAO & Funding 分类下，但两者是两个完全不同的资助项目：运作方式、资助金额、预期目标等都完全不同。

为了保持讨论的集中性，在另一篇帖子中对 Spark 和 DAO 二者差异进行了浅析，也向社区简单汇报 Spark 的运营近况。

关于DAO对特定类似提案的资助侧重，以下为最合适的推进路径：

Spark 和 Community Fund DAO 资助的差异浅析

DAO 本身也不会主动出资赞助某个项目或赛事。所以社区如果认为特定类型项目更值得支持，最合适的方式就有人提出这类提案，大家投票支持。如果想把对特定类型的资助倾斜变成制度，比如设立专项额度，则属于元规则修改，可以通过发起元规则提案的方式推进。

此外，Crowns 如果有合适的部分工作想申请Spark，Spark 委员会非常欢迎，但是否获批仍要看具体提案，尤其是范围是否控制在Spark定位以内。申请方式请见 Spark 主帖。

Best,

posts.name: chioma christopher
posts.cooked:
Thanks Thinker, these are good points.

I like the idea of driver races as a second kind of race, next to the normal ones where you drive yourself. In a driver race you wouldn’t steer. Everyone would get the same driver, built into the game, and nobody writes their own bot. The only difference is how you tune it before the race, how sharp it turns, when it brakes, which item it goes for, when it boosts. Then the game drives the car for you.

A tuned driver could also race people who drive by hand in the same race. Whoever finishes first wins, and the chain checks the result the same way for both.

Everyone’s settings could stay hidden until all players have joined, so nobody can copy the best setup at the last second. Speed should cost something too. Boosting could make the car turn worse and cost health, so no single setup always wins.

The random obstacles fit well with this. Rocks on the road could be placed using a block that is mined after everyone has joined, so nobody knows where they’ll be when they join, not even me. Every race would be a bit different, so you can’t just tune for one fixed track. My mentor suggested taking randomness from a later block before, and I used it in an earlier game.

Later, the driver could be a Spore with its settings inside and its wins recorded on chain, so a good driver has a history anyone can see. what do you think?

Thanks for the DAO idea as well. And thanks @zz_tovarishch for explaining DAO vs Spark, I’ll read the Spark post.

posts.name: Thinker
posts.cooked:
上贴发的有些匆忙，中间有几处错误（已修改）。也感谢 @zz_tovarishch 的解释。

这个游戏我只进入页面，但并没有去试玩（因为我不是游戏爱好者）。我也并不清楚项目情况。

只是看到社区资助项目多数在工具端，建议可以适当关注下应用类项目，尤其是社区自行完成的优质项目，可以用可行的间接方式的帮其度下冷启动期。

当然应用类项目必须要有自己的盈利模式，而不是去依赖社区的资助存活。资助模式更希望是以赞助/提供流动性等方面的参与，并不是对还未成型的应用方案文档来资助。
